top.line: How to help: six steps for anyone who wants to be involved with sgit, Risk Mandate or this newsroom.
top.para: The best help is to use what we build and say honestly what happened. Say hello to agent@riskmandate.ai, set up Claude and GitHub, try one thing in each place, publish what you did, check in, and take the next task when you have time. In return: your work in public, learning, and credibility. Every site should have this page.

in-short.line: Seven lines: use it, say hello, set up, try each place, publish and check in, no commitment, a win-win.
in-short.para: Using what we build is the best help. One email puts you on the list. A Claude account, GitHub and a repository. One thing each in Risk Mandate, sgit and the newsroom. Links and honest feedback. We send tasks; do them when you can. The open source deal: your work in public.

question.line: More people ask how they can help; the answer is to use what we build, as it is today.
question.para: Some want to learn, some to help, some a job or a next challenge. Until people outside the team create vaults, follow the Claude and GitHub setup and try new capabilities, we are not really testing. Helpers differ from the first customers with credit and milestones, though the groups overlap.

steps.line: Six steps: say hello, set up your tools, try one thing in each place, publish, check in, take the next task.
steps.para: Email agent@riskmandate.ai with your interest and consent to contact. Claude Code, GitHub, one repository. Risk Mandate's six examples, sgit in the browser or pip, and the newsroom's credit, vault and notes. A site or vault we can open. What you did, what got in the way, what is next. Tasks are optional.

winwin.line: A win-win, the open source way: time, use and honest feedback, for visibility, learning and credibility.
winwin.para: Helpers give time when they have it, use what we build with its rough edges, and send links and honest feedback. They get their work credited in public, a place to learn real work with agents, vaults and policies, references, and early access with a say. What you publish is your portfolio.

gravity.line: What we learn from each helper: their centre of gravity, where instructions held, and where they stopped.
gravity.para: sgit, Risk Mandate, the newsroom or all three; what they did without help and what surprised us. The customer site tracks milestones; for helpers it starts lighter, with the inbox agent's record and check-ins, and it tells us where to put effort and which tasks to send next.

brief.line: The brief: a how-to-help page on every site and in every README, one list, and synthetic users on the same path.
brief.para: Each site links a how-to-help page from its front page and footer, with its first task; each repository's README carries the steps, as this newsroom's now does; everyone goes on one list. Our synthetic users walk the six steps daily: they find what breaks, people find what confuses.

limits.line: Voluntary and unpaid; not a job offer; the steps will change; the brief is a proposal.
limits.para: Helping has no time commitment, and reading credit is not money. It is a place to start and be seen. Tasks and links will move as we ship, and this page will follow. Only this newsroom's README has the steps so far.

sources.line: My voice memo, and the pages the steps point to on the customer site, sgit.ai and this newsroom.
sources.para: The memo of 21 October 2026; the start-here page, examples, milestones and reviews on customers.riskmandate.ai; sgit in the browser; the newsroom's reader credit and vault; the inbox at agent@riskmandate.ai; and related articles on first customers, the inbox, the agentic inbox and synthetic users.
